tier_a.name: Context7
tier_a.why_now: This is the cleanest immediate upgrade for current-doc and API lookup inside Cursor.
tier_a.gap_filled: Repo-scale and documentation-scale retrieval is still weaker than the project's research standard demands.
tier_a.complements_or_supersedes: ResearchAgent, SkillLibrary semantic retrieval, and rg-based repo exploration.
tier_a.pilot_experiment: Use Context7 on 10 repo questions involving fast-moving libraries or APIs and compare answer freshness versus current shell-plus-web lookup.
tier_a.risk_note: Low security risk; main risk is treating vendor-curated docs as complete.
tier_a.feasibility_note: Plugin-era Cursor already exists locally, so the main cost is install/auth rather than version gating.

tier_a.name: Parallel
tier_a.why_now: The repo already emphasizes pre-execution research, and Parallel adds a strong external research surface inside Cursor.
tier_a.gap_filled: Structured deep research and content extraction remain external to the main Cursor loop.
tier_a.complements_or_supersedes: ResearchAgent and the project's context-locked research prompts.
tier_a.pilot_experiment: Run the same literature-and-docs task with Parallel and the existing manual web path, then compare source breadth, citation quality, and time-to-brief.
tier_a.risk_note: Moderate risk of overcollection or noisy research results if not scoped tightly.
tier_a.feasibility_note: Usable on the current local Cursor baseline, but requires external service setup.

tier_a.name: Playwright
tier_a.why_now: The project is a browser- and GUI-heavy agent runtime; Playwright is the highest-signal external MCP augmentation for browser execution and testing.
tier_a.gap_filled: Current browser control is local-macOS-first and Safari-centric. A parallel browser automation surface would add controllable, testable browser execution.
tier_a.complements_or_supersedes: web_primitives.py, VerificationGate, VisualMonitor, and the universal-agent path.
tier_a.pilot_experiment: Add a sandboxed Playwright MCP config and compare one site task against the current local web path on determinism, observability, and failure recovery.
tier_a.risk_note: Medium security risk because browser automation expands reachable surface area and requires clear sandbox discipline.
tier_a.feasibility_note: Current local Cursor can use stdio MCP servers; this is a setup question, not a 2.6 feature gate.

tier_a.name: Langfuse
tier_a.why_now: The repo already invests heavily in traces, summaries, evaluation, and run forensics; Langfuse matches that center of gravity directly.
tier_a.gap_filled: There is no Cursor-native external tracing and prompt/eval surface woven into the current workflow.
tier_a.complements_or_supersedes: TraceWriter, Summarizer, BenchmarkEvaluator, and diagnostic artifacts.
tier_a.pilot_experiment: Instrument a small set of research or planning tasks with Langfuse and compare whether prompt/version/run visibility improves postmortem quality.
tier_a.risk_note: Low-to-medium risk; the main concern is export of sensitive run context to an external service.
tier_a.feasibility_note: Usable on the current local baseline with plugin setup and Langfuse access.

tier_a.name: Runlayer
tier_a.why_now: If this repo adopts more MCPs, governance becomes a first-order concern rather than a later cleanup step.
tier_a.gap_filled: Current repo security is strong inside the Python runtime, but there is no dedicated Cursor-side MCP governance and audit surface.
tier_a.complements_or_supersedes: security/sanitizer.py, CredentialVault, HostToolHealth, and HITL patterns.
tier_a.pilot_experiment: Install Runlayer in a disposable environment and test whether it materially improves MCP discovery, auditability, secret handling, and policy visibility.
tier_a.risk_note: Medium risk because it becomes part of the MCP control plane; its own trust boundary must be reviewed carefully.
tier_a.feasibility_note: Usable on current Cursor with setup; no 2.6-only dependency is required for core value.

tier_a.name: concentric-trace-mcp
tier_a.why_now: The repo already has rich traces; exposing them cleanly to Cursor would convert latent research assets into interactive workflow power.
tier_a.gap_filled: Trace inspection is currently script- or file-driven rather than native to Cursor's MCP tool loop.
tier_a.pilot_experiment: Prototype read_run_manifest, list_recent_runs, and summarize_failure_chain as MCP tools and compare debugging speed against file-only inspection.
tier_a.risk_note: Low risk if read-only; medium if any mutation or redaction boundaries are weak.
tier_a.feasibility_note: No local Cursor version blocker; requires building and registering the MCP server.

tier_a.name: concentric-benchmark-mcp
tier_a.why_now: The project already contains benchmark and claims-based evaluation machinery; Cursor should be able to query and compare runs directly.
tier_a.gap_filled: Evaluation remains too file-centric for rapid iterative decision-making in Cursor.
tier_a.pilot_experiment: Prototype evaluate_run and compare_runs MCP tools, then use them during one regression-analysis cycle.
tier_a.risk_note: Low risk if tools are read-only and scoped to repo-local data.
tier_a.feasibility_note: Requires server implementation, not a Cursor upgrade.

tier_a.name: concentric-health-mcp
tier_a.why_now: Environment drift and tool-health regressions are already first-order failure modes in this project.
tier_a.gap_filled: Host readiness and baseline drift checks are not available as a native Cursor tool surface.
tier_a.pilot_experiment: Prototype health_summary, check_tool_class, and compare_environment_baselines MCP tools and use them before live runs.
tier_a.risk_note: Low risk; the main concern is leaking unnecessary host detail into prompts or logs.

tier_a.name: concentric-research-mcp
tier_a.why_now: ResearchAgent is already a differentiated internal capability; surfacing it via MCP would make it reusable from inside Cursor without bespoke wrappers.
tier_a.gap_filled: Research briefs and source registers are generated in the repo but not exposed as a reusable tool surface to Cursor.
tier_a.complements_or_supersedes: ResearchAgent, ResearchBrief artifacts, and context-locked research prompts.
tier_a.pilot_experiment: Prototype run_research_brief and fetch_research_context MCP tools for one complex pre-execution task.
tier_a.risk_note: Low-to-medium risk depending on web-search scope and prompt-budget control.
tier_a.feasibility_note: Needs implementation, but no local version gate.

tier_b.name: Sentry
tier_b.why_now: Strong fit for debugging and failure forensics, but slightly less central than traces/eval already native to the repo.
tier_b.gap_filled: External error tracking and incident review.
tier_b.pilot_experiment: Use Sentry on one failing integration or runtime incident and compare time-to-root-cause against current methods.
tier_b.risk_note: External telemetry boundary must be reviewed.
tier_b.feasibility_note: Usable on the current local Cursor baseline with setup.

tier_b.name: GitHub
tier_b.why_now: Useful for PR/issues/review workflows, but the repo already has strong git and shell access.
tier_b.gap_filled: Structured GitHub workflow actions inside MCP.
tier_b.complements_or_supersedes: git CLI and future review-loop automation.
tier_b.pilot_experiment: Use GitHub MCP for one issue-to-branch-to-review loop and compare the clarity versus shell-only flow.
tier_b.risk_note: Repository mutation risk requires scoped tokens and repo boundaries.
tier_b.feasibility_note: Usable on the current local Cursor baseline with Docker/token setup.

tier_b.name: Browserbase
tier_b.why_now: This is a credible browser-compute augmentation, but Playwright is the cleaner first browser MCP pilot.
tier_b.complements_or_supersedes: Playwright-style browser automation and web task experiments.
tier_b.pilot_experiment: Compare one Browserbase MCP flow against a Playwright MCP flow for setup cost and useful observability.
tier_b.risk_note: External browser execution broadens the data-handling boundary.
tier_b.feasibility_note: Usable on the current version with setup.

tier_b.name: Cursor Team Kit
tier_b.why_now: Strong dev-loop automation ideas, but more valuable after the core research, trace, and health surfaces are in place.
tier_b.gap_filled: CI, code review, and shipping workflow automation inside Cursor.
tier_b.complements_or_supersedes: Future code-review automation and shipping workflows.
tier_b.pilot_experiment: Use Cursor Team Kit on one small code-review or CI-fix loop in a disposable branch.
tier_b.risk_note: Potential overlap with project-specific workflow needs.
tier_b.feasibility_note: Plugin-era feature; requires setup, not a 2.6-only surface.

tier_b.name: Figma
tier_b.why_now: Relevant for artifact generation and visual review, and the local Cursor build is now new enough to test the MCP Apps path directly.
tier_b.gap_filled: Visual artifact and diagram collaboration inside Cursor.
tier_b.pilot_experiment: Use Figma MCP Apps output in one artifact-review task on local Cursor 2.6.11 and compare it with the existing screenshot/reference-board workflow.
tier_b.risk_note: Low risk; the main issue is whether the workflow actually benefits from in-chat visual UI.
tier_b.feasibility_note: Local Cursor 2.6.11 is new enough to test both the plugin and MCP Apps experience; remaining work is setup and Figma-side enablement.

tier_b.name: tldraw
tier_b.why_now: The local Cursor build is now new enough to test MCP Apps whiteboarding directly instead of treating it as a future-only surface.
tier_b.pilot_experiment: Use tldraw MCP Apps on local Cursor 2.6.11 for one planning or debugging whiteboard experiment and compare it with the current reference-board path.
tier_b.risk_note: Low risk; main concern is whether it adds signal over existing reference-board artifacts.
tier_b.feasibility_note: Local Cursor 2.6.11 is new enough to test the MCP Apps experience directly; remaining work is plugin setup and workflow validation.

tier_b.name: Amplitude
tier_b.why_now: The local Cursor build is now new enough to test MCP Apps chart review directly rather than treating it as version-blocked.
tier_b.gap_filled: Interactive chart and dashboard review inside Cursor.
tier_b.pilot_experiment: Test one Amplitude MCP Apps chart-review flow on local Cursor 2.6.11 and see whether it improves evidence review over current artifacts.
tier_b.risk_note: Low risk; limited by local version and workflow fit.
tier_b.feasibility_note: Local Cursor 2.6.11 is new enough to test the MCP Apps path directly; remaining work is plugin setup and validating workflow fit.

tier_b.name: Atlassian
tier_b.why_now: Good coordination surface, but valuable only if the workflow starts leaning harder into Jira/Confluence-based planning and triage.
tier_b.complements_or_supersedes: Future team workflows, not the current single-repo research bottleneck.
tier_b.pilot_experiment: Try Atlassian on one planning/triage loop if Jira/Confluence becomes active in the workflow.
tier_b.risk_note: Medium risk due to access scope and data boundary.
tier_b.feasibility_note: Usable on the current version with OAuth setup.

tier_b.name: concentric-visual-monitor-mcp
tier_b.why_now: Valuable, but secondary to trace, benchmark, and health surfaces.
tier_b.gap_filled: Cursor-native access to screenshot timelines and drift deltas.
tier_b.pilot_experiment: Expose last_n_timeline and compare_against_reference tools for one failure-analysis workflow.
tier_b.risk_note: Careful screenshot redaction boundaries are required.

tier_b.name: concentric-skill-mcp
tier_b.why_now: Skill retrieval is valuable, but it sits behind stronger immediate needs like traces and health.
tier_b.gap_filled: Expose semantic skill retrieval and maturity-gated reuse to Cursor.
tier_b.pilot_experiment: Prototype retrieve_skills and inspect_skill MCP tools and compare planning quality on repeated task families.
tier_b.risk_note: Low risk; main concern is surfacing stale or overtrusted skills.
